mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate level (FEDFUNDS < 0.2%) compresses equity discount rates, consistently generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate to below 0.2% triggers monetary easing, reducing equity discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS falls below 0.2%, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in industrial production (INDPRO) and GDP (GDPC1) above 0.5% monthly signals robust economic expansion, increasing corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate > 0.5% and INDPRO growth rate > 0.5%
failure_condition: When both GDPC1 and INDPRO growth rates exceed 0.5%, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a high labor market tightness regime (UNRATE < 5.0%), rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) triggers monetary tightening expectations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 5.0% and CPIAUCSL rises, S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS growth rate > 0.5% monthly) supports corporate profitability, consistently generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth rate exceeds 0.5%, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 9.0% signals economic distress and potential for policy stimulus, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 9.0%, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS < 0.2%) and rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL > 215) indicates a supportive monetary policy environment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 215 and FEDFUNDS < 0.2, S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: In an early-cycle expansion regime (HOUST growth rate > 0.5%), rising housing starts signal strong consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST growth rate exceeds 0.5%, S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such instances.
